meta.name: RPSGT Scoring Lab Phase 3 event-boundary pack
meta.sourceBasis: Original Sleep Pathways Guild teaching signals created to practice continuous respiratory-reduction placement and counting across 30-second display boundaries. AASM Scoring Manual Version 3 governs actual apnea, hypopnea, and RERA classification.
meta.clinicalBoundary: This pack tests onset, continuity, recovery, and annotation placement only. The generic airflow reductions are candidate events and are not presented as fully classified apneas or hypopneas unless all required Version 3 criteria are supplied elsewhere. Epoch boundaries organize the display; they do not divide one continuous physiologic reduction into separate events.
meta.governingAuthority: AASM Scoring Manual Version 3, Section VIII Part 1: Adult Respiratory Rules, especially event-duration measurement
visualCorroboration: Gupta, R., Pandi-Perumal, S. R., & BaHammam, A. S. (2018). Clinical atlas of polysomnography. Apple Academic Press.
Geyer, J. D., Carney, P. R., & Payne, T. A. (2010). Atlas of polysomnography (2nd ed.). Lippincott Williams & Wilkins.

cases.title: One reduction across the first boundary
cases.prompt: Count the distinct candidate airflow reductions, then mark the reduction that continues from Epoch 1 into Epoch 2.
cases.focus: The 30-second divider crosses the reduction, but the underlying airflow change remains continuous.
cases.rationale: The airflow reduction begins before 0:30 and recovers after 0:30 without returning toward baseline at the divider. Treat it as one continuous candidate reduction for placement practice. Actual event classification requires the complete Version 3 criteria.

cases.title: Two reductions with one crossing 1:00
cases.prompt: Count all distinct candidate airflow reductions, then mark the reduction that crosses from Epoch 2 into Epoch 3.
cases.focus: Separate reductions are divided by a clear return toward baseline; an epoch divider alone is not a separator.
cases.rationale: There are two distinct reductions because airflow recovers between them. The second begins before 1:00 and continues after 1:00, so it remains one continuous candidate reduction across the display boundary.

cases.title: Boundary reduction followed by a separate reduction
cases.prompt: Count the distinct candidate airflow reductions, then mark the reduction that crosses the 0:30 boundary.
cases.focus: Use recovery of the physiologic signal—not the epoch label—to decide where one reduction ends and another can begin.
cases.rationale: The first reduction remains continuous through 0:30 and recovers near 0:43. A separate later reduction begins after a substantial return toward baseline, producing two candidate reductions total.

cases.title: Three reductions with a middle boundary crossing
cases.prompt: Count all distinct candidate airflow reductions, then mark the middle reduction that continues across the 1:00 boundary.
cases.focus: Track onset, continuity, and recovery through all three epochs before deciding the count.
cases.rationale: Three reductions are separated by clear recovery. The middle reduction crosses 1:00 without recovering at the divider, so it remains one continuous candidate reduction rather than becoming two.
